title: The quotes change everything
idea: "5" is text and 5 is a number. Same-looking, but the computer stores and uses them differently.

exercises.explanation: No quotes means numbers. The computer does the math: 5 + 3 is 8.
These are text. For text, + JOINS the pieces: "5" and "3" become "53". Same symbol, very different result!

exercises.prompt: The + symbol does the same thing whether the values are text or numbers.
exercises.explanation: No! On numbers + ADDS (5 + 3 = 8). On text + JOINS ("5" + "3" = "53"). This is the heart of the bug we're learning to avoid.

exercises.prompt: Which of these would the computer ADD to get 15?
exercises.explanation: Only 7 + 8 (both numbers) gets added to 15. "7" + "8" would join into "78" instead.
Joining text glues it with no space: catdog. (You'd add " " yourself if you wanted a space.)

exercises.prompt: Select EVERY line that does number math (adds), not text joining.
exercises.explanation: Lines without quotes work on numbers and add (12 and 12). The quoted ones join text instead.

exercises.prompt:
score = "10"
bonus = "5"
print(score + bonus)

What shows?
exercises.explanation: Both variables hold TEXT (quotes!). + joins them: "10" + "5" is "105", not 15. A classic surprise.

exercises.prompt:
score = 10
bonus = 5
print(score + bonus)

What shows?
exercises.explanation: No quotes this time — real numbers. + adds them: 10 + 5 = 15. The only change from before was removing the quotes.

exercises.prompt: Match each line to what it shows.
exercises.explanation: Numbers add (4). Text joins (22, abcd). Reading the quotes tells you which will happen.

exercises.prompt: If you MEAN to add numbers but your values are text, you'll get a joined result instead of a sum.
exercises.explanation: Exactly — that's the 'added text instead of numbers' bug. The fix is converting the type, which starts next lesson.
